text:
One day you will arrive with a frailty of love,
tender as dew,
impetuous as rain,
the bronze of the sun on your skin,
the hum
of the breeze in your murmurs,
and you will alight with the elegance of a mountain flower.


You will arrive with your slender, expressive arms,
your head tilted
in a way no sculptor has ever captured,
and shades spoken by shoulder and neck,
your
face with the will to pass and pass again,
as many times as the skies in
delicate change
of clouds and blues and flickering sun.



Except that
perhaps you will not arrive, oh dream girl,
perhaps we will only
cross paths as the world turns
and take from a glance into the eyes
a film of hope and a
day to remember.



* * *


Dreams at twilight
Dreams at twilight,
dreams only at the end of day
that, as day
falls, return
to gray things, to darkness,
to what is distant
and deep,
to the land of dreams.


Dreams, dreams only at twilight,
only old photographs,
remembered,
of lost days when the loss of day
with
tears wrote the loss of the heart.


So may tears and losses and broken dreams
find your heart at
twilight.

translation.title: Dream Girl
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering of Carl Sandburg. The supplied Spanish combines the dream-girl poem with ‘Dreams at Twilight’; both headings, repetitions, and visual transitions are preserved.
